To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the backlogging and the load-building processes have a significant impact on the performance of the system; (ii) the performance can be significantly improved by using a FIFO rule for backlogging and a FIFO or an LPT rule for load-building; and (iii) the performance can also be improved by using a LPT rule for backlogging.
the backorder processing rule has a significant effect on the performance of a multi-echelons inventory network.

(1) the lead-time at the retailer level can be significantly affected by the choice of backlogging and load building processing rules, (2) the lead-time performance of the system can be significantly improved by using a load-building processing rule that is different than the backlogging processing rule, and (3) the performance improvement can be achieved without increasing the inventory levels at the retailer level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of backlog and load-building queues in an inventory system with multiple echelons.
the development of new modeling approaches and simulation techniques for the evaluation of the performance of a two-echelon, multi-echelon, inventory system.
the effects of different processing rules for backlogging and load building on the performance of a two-echelon supply chain.
